To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the circular polarization of photoluminescence from single layers of MoX2 (X=S, Se) is initialized as the energy of the excitation pulse is varied and that the depolarization of the emitted light is caused by phonon-assisted exciton scattering between the two valleys at the K-point.
the depolarization threshold energy is the same for neutral and charged excitations in both materials, and that this threshold energy is twice the energy of the LA phonon in both materials.

(i) the threshold for depolarization is twice the LA phononic energy, (ii) the depolarization rate increases with increasing energy above the threshold, and (iii) the depolarized fraction saturates at a value that is close to 100% within 100 meV of the threshold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the optical polarization of the photoluminescence in single layer MoS2 and the intervalley scattering of the excitons.
optical polarization of excitons in single layers of the semiconductors MoS2 and WSe2.
the optical polarization of the excitons and the depolarization of these excitons in the presence of phonons in MoS2 and in MoSe2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the depolarization of the excitonic luminescence in the single layers of MoX2 (X= S or Se) is caused by the intervalley scattering of the excited excitons.
the intervalley scattering of an exciton with excess energy is the main cause of depolarization in single-layer MoS2 and single-layer MoSe2.
the intervalley scattering of the exciton is a key factor for the depolarization of the photoluminescence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the depolarization of the optical emission in MoS2 and its isoelectronic analog MoSe2 can be attributed to the intervalley scattering of the exciton, which is mediated by the LO and LA optical phonons.
in MoS2 and in MoSe2 the intervalley scattering is phonon-assisted, with a phonon energy of 50 and 40 meV, respectively.
the intervalley scattering in MoS2 and in MoSe2 are similar and the threshold energy of the depolarizing intervalley scattering is determined by the LA phonon in the material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the depolarization is due to the energy-dependent intervalley scattering and not due to the energy-independent spin relaxation.
, for a given material, a universal threshold energy exists for the onset of intervalley scattering, which is independent of whether the excitation is a neutral or charged exciton.
the intervalley scattering is not phonon-assisted, as has been previously thought, but is rather a result of the excess kinetic energy of the excited state.
